I am an old woman now, seventy-six years, and this small maize plot near my house is what I tend myself with help from my grandchildren. I have no money for the chemical fertilizer from the cooperative this year, so I will spread the manure from my few animals like I always do, and save the seed I kept from last harvest. My legs are slow, so my family must do most of the weeding, and if the rains are weak I can only carry water by jerrycan from the spring — I cannot really irrigate this land.
